key_insight: HVOF-sprayed Ni-20Cr+40TiC produced the best high-temperature oxidation resistance on SA516 boiler steel, cutting maximum weight gain by 95.71% versus bare steel.
engineering_relevance: For boiler and high-temperature service, dense Ni-Cr ceramic coatings can substantially improve oxide-scale protection, especially when applied by HVOF rather than plasma spray.
method: SA516 steel was coated with Ni-20Cr, Ni-20Cr+40TiC, and Ni-20Cr+40TiN using HVOF and plasma spray.
Cyclic oxidation testing was run for 50 cycles at 900°C in air.
XRD, SEM/EDS, and X-ray mapping were used to track phase and microstructural changes.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports the uncoated steel suffered severe spalling and cracking, while the HVOF Ni-20Cr+40TiC coating showed the lowest weight gain and a protective oxide mix of Cr2O3, TiO2, NiTiO4, and NiO.
watch_item: Performance is demonstrated under laboratory cyclic oxidation; long-term field behavior, thermal-shock durability, and coating adhesion under service loads still need validation.
paper_title: Microstructure and High-Temperature Oxidation Behaviour of HVOF and Plasma Sprayed Ni–Cr-Based Ceramic Coatings on SA516 Boiler Steel
